claim: The buoyant force is the net upward force on any object in a fluid.
evidence_text: [cal-009-a0-c1-e1] The buoyant force is the net upward force on any object in any fluid.

claim: An object remains suspended at a depth when the buoyant force on it is greater than its weight.
evidence_text: [cal-009-a0-c2-e1] If the buoyant force is greater than the object's weight, the object will rise to the surface and float. If the buoyant force is less than the object's weight, the object will sink. If the buoyant force equals the object's weight, the object will remain suspended at that depth. The buoyant force is always present whether the object floats, sinks, or is suspended in a fluid.
